title: Which primes stay prime when you double them and add 1?
description: Primes from the list are doubled and one is added, and each result is looked up in the list of primes. Five primes are found that give another prime.
teaching_notes: One idea: double the prime, add one, and keep it only when the result is in the list of primes. Watch for students who think the rule works for every prime.

video_script.why: The child tries primes from the list, doubles them, adds one and looks the result up in the same list.
video_script.substitution: Double a prime from the list, add one and look the result up in the list.
video_script.anchor: The list of primes with an arrow machine that doubles a prime and adds one
video_script.payoff_line: Yes, there are more such primes. Five, eleven, twenty three, twenty nine and forty one all work.
video_script.design: A machine takes in a prime, doubles it, adds one, and gives out a number; the output is looked up in the list and turns teal when it is a prime and amber when it is not.

beats.on_screen: title card From your book; the machine with 3 going in and 7 coming out; the words double and add 1

marks.machine: three goes into the machine and seven comes out
marks.ask: a question mark appears for other primes

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about doubling primes.
<bookmark mark='machine'/>Three is a prime, and two times three plus one is seven, which is also a prime.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Are there other primes like this? Find at least five.

beats.on_screen: the machine stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: prime in, then × 2, then + 1, then look the result up in the list of primes

marks.steps: the machine steps double, add one and look up appear in order
marks.list: the list of primes is shown for looking up

narration: <bookmark mark='steps'/>Double a prime, add one, and you get a new number.
<bookmark mark='list'/>We look the new number up in the list of primes from the circling and crossing out.

beats.on_screen: Given: the primes up to 100; 2 × 3 + 1 = 7 is a prime

marks.given: the list of primes and the first example are written

narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, the list of primes, and the example that three gives seven.

beats.on_screen: To find: 5 primes whose double plus 1 is also a prime

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to find five more primes that behave like three.

marks.fivein: five goes through the machine and eleven comes out in teal
marks.elevenin: eleven goes through the machine and twenty three comes out in teal

narration: <bookmark mark='fivein'/>Step one, try the primes in order. Two times five plus one is eleven, and eleven is on the list.
<bookmark mark='elevenin'/>Two times eleven plus one is twenty three, and twenty three is on the list too.

marks.twenty: twenty three gives forty seven in teal
marks.twentynine: twenty nine gives fifty nine in teal
marks.forty: forty one gives eighty three in teal

narration: <bookmark mark='twenty'/>Step two, try more. Twenty three gives forty seven, which is on the list.
<bookmark mark='twentynine'/>Twenty nine gives fifty nine, which is on the list.
<bookmark mark='forty'/>Forty one gives eighty three, which is on the list as well.

beats.on_screen: Check: 2 × 7 + 1 = 15 = 3 × 5, not prime; so the rule does not work for every prime

marks.sevenin: seven goes through the machine and fifteen comes out in amber
marks.list: fifteen splits into three times five

narration: <bookmark mark='sevenin'/>Step three, check that the list decides each case. Seven gives fifteen, which is three times five, so seven does not work.
<bookmark mark='list'/>The rule works for some primes only, and the list tells us which.

beats.on_screen: Answer: Yes. 5, 11, 23, 29, 41 each give a prime
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Yes, there are more such primes. Five, eleven, twenty three, twenty nine and forty one all work.
